- Overestimate early in the forecast horizon, especially after sharp price spikes; reduce initial forecast values.
- Underestimate in the final 5–10 days of the forecast; adjust upward to reflect mean reversion toward recent trend.
- Overshoot after a spike by 5–15% in the immediate next period; apply a dampening factor to prevent overcorrection.
- Model tends to lag behind true price movements by 1–3 days; shift forecast slightly ahead of actual price peaks.
- When history shows strong upward momentum, model often fails to capture the full extent of the rally; increase forecast by 2–5% for the next 3–5 days.
- Avoid overfitting to recent high values; if last 5–7 days are high, reduce forecast for next period to avoid “peak inflation” bias.
- If forecast is consistently 5–10% above true outcome, reduce baseline by 3–5% and apply a smoothing filter to reduce volatility amplification.
